resources.string: This build can discover and securely pair. The connection service and the pairing screen arrive in M2.
Identity fingerprint %1$s. Both devices must show the same six-digit code before either trusts the other.
The device identity could not be loaded on this build. See Help.
Milestone M1 adds the secure connectivity core: mutual TLS with pinned keys, the session handshake, and pairing. The connection service and on-device pairing screen arrive in M2/M4.
Klyndro talks only to your own devices on your own network. There is no account and no cloud service.
Pairing shows a six-digit code that must match on both devices before anything is trusted. The pairing screen is not built yet.
Available once the transport lands in M1.
Klyndro asks for nothing by default. Each capability below is requested only when you turn the matching feature on.
Granted at install time. Used for discovery and the pairing connection.

Android 10 and later block clipboard access for apps that are not in the foreground or set as the keyboard. Klyndro cannot read your clipboard silently in the background; see Help for the supported fallbacks.
A sensitive, user-granted system permission. It will be requested in M5, and only if you enable forwarding.
Preferences are stored now; synchronization itself arrives in M2.
The connection service arrives in M4. HyperOS also needs manual autostart and battery settings; see Help.
Keeps the link to your paired Mac alive.
No paired Mac with a known address
Android is not letting Klyndro read the clipboard right now. Keep this screen open and try again.
Android only allows clipboard access while Klyndro is on screen, so sync runs while this app is open. This is a platform restriction, not a setting.
Start pairing on the Mac first: open Klyndro and choose “Pair a device…”. Then tap the Mac below.
No Mac found yet. Both devices must be on the same Wi-Fi network.
%1$s must show the same six digits. Only confirm if they match.
Open Settings → Apps → Klyndro → Battery and choose "No restrictions". In Security → Autostart, allow Klyndro. Without these, HyperOS may stop background work even when Android allows it.

Android only lets the focused app, or the active keyboard, read the clipboard. Klyndro plans a share-sheet action and a quick-settings tile so copying stays one tap, and will document exactly which path works on your device.
Mirroring uses scrcpy on the Mac and needs USB debugging or wireless debugging enabled on the phone. It arrives in M3.
